summary_plain: Moves about 31 arcseconds per hour across 25 images over 47.2 hours. It matches the known asteroid 570 Kythera (A905 OF).

orbit.reported_orbit: The arc is too short to fix one orbit, so this is the most circular of the 258 sampled orbits that fit the detections; the clones show the range.

known_object.observer: SPHEREx (geocentric JPL predictions corrected with the spacecraft position from the FITS headers)

scores.definition: Rule-based ranking score in [0, 1]: motion_consistency x snr x (1 - artifact_likelihood). It orders candidates for review. It is not a probability.

explanation.text: Detected in 25 SPHEREx exposures spanning 47.2 hours. It moves 30.8 arcseconds per hour toward position angle 65 degrees. A straight-line fit leaves 2.06 arcseconds of scatter. Its faintest detection has a signal-to-noise ratio of 20.8. Its positions match JPL's prediction for 570 Kythera (A905 OF) to within 1.1 arcseconds at every epoch.

history.change: linked 25 detections over 4 visits from 2026-06-11 to 2026-06-13

disclaimer: An unmatched candidate may be an imaging artifact, a measurement error, or an object missing from the catalogs we checked. This is not a discovery claim.
